newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end higher in holiday-type trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end higher in holiday-type trade.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended higher in light pre-holiday trade with Eurodollars ending near the day's highs after the market caught a light bid into the close, traders said.

December T-bonds also ended with a slight bid when the bond and note futures closed at 1210 CDT/1710 GMT in observance of the U.S. Columbus Day holiday on Monday. Bond and note futures will be closed on Monday, while Eurodollar pit trade will end at 1200 CDT/1700 GMT.
After a week of corrective price action, the market finally attempted to test the highs of October 4.
December T-bonds rose to 110-25/32 in reaction to the September Producer Price Index (PPI) and retail sales, which did not rise as much as the market had priced in on Thursday.
While September retail sales' rise of 0.7 percent was higher than Reuters' average trade estimate of up 0.2 percent, the market highlighted some forecasts for a 1.3 percent increase.
"Traders were really afraid of much higher numbers," one Eurodollar futures trader said.
March Eurodollars ended near the daily high at 94.30.
Offers at the 94.30 to 94.31 area prevented locals from pushing prices much higher, they said.
December T-bonds rose to 110-25/32 after one large U.S. firm bought 2,500 contracts and caused shorts to cover positions.
Traders said the market found light buyers after Federal Reserve governor Lawrence Lindsey said real income growth was "virtually nonexistant."
On Monday, the weekly BTM/Schroders sales index and the September Atlanta Federal Reserve index will be released ahead of the key September consumer price index (CPI) on Tuesday.

At the end of pit trade, December T-bonds were up 18/32 at 110-19/32, 10-year notes were up 12/32 at 108-07/32, March T-bills were up nine basis points at 94.81, December Eurodollars were up four bps at 94.35, and March Eurodollars were eight bps higher at 94.28. -Derivative desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivative@reuter.com
